item.title: Mitsubishi UBE Cement Is Said to Plan for December Tokyo Listing
item.description: Mitsubishi UBE Cement Corp. is planning to go public as soon as December, according to people familiar with the matter, five years after being formed through units of Japanese materials companies.

item.title: China’s Official Newspaper Warns US Over Expanding Tech Curbs
item.description: The official newspaper of China’s ruling Communist Party warned of countermeasures against widening US technology curbs as Washington considers banning imports of some Chinese AI components, adding a fresh source of strain to the countries’ fragile trade truce.

item.title: Thai Inflation Eases to 1.95% in July, Slows for Third Month
item.description: Thailand’s inflation unexpectedly eased for a third straight month, bolstering the central bank’s view that it can keep interest rates on hold to support the economy.

item.title: Thailand Rules Out Fully Owned SpaceX Venture in US Trade Talks
item.description: Thailand won’t allow US firms to establish fully foreign-owned satellite telecoms as part of trade talks with the Trump administration, resisting such investments in the sector over sovereignty issues, said the country’s vice commerce minister.

item.title: New Zealand’s Plan to Move to Annual Census Hits Political Hurdle
item.description: New Zealand’s statistics agency may need to run the next five-yearly census in 2028 after all as a plan to defer it and revert to annual surveys from 2030 runs into political hurdles.

item.title: China’s AI Agent Unicorn Lovart Is Said to Explore Hong Kong IPO
item.description: Evoken, the Chinese startup behind AI design agent Lovart, is considering an initial public offering in Hong Kong, people familiar with the matter said, the latest such firm seeking to tap booming investor demand for artificial intelligence tools after the breakout success of Manus.

item.title: SK Hynix Climbs as Investors Bet on Shareholder Return Plan
item.description: Shares of SK Hynix Inc. advanced, lifted by an overnight rally in US chipmakers and speculation that the Korean firm may soon unveil buybacks and other details of a broader shareholder return plan.

item.title: LIC’s Big Share Sale Draws Investors Even as India’s IPO Market Stalls
item.description: India expands the size of the offering to raise $3.3 billion amid strong demand.

item.title: Temasek, Morgan Stanley Are Said to Eye Adtek Pre-IPO Investment
item.description: Shenzhen Adtek Technology Co. is close to raising up to 2 billion yuan ($296 million) in a private fundraising round ahead of its planned initial public offering in Hong Kong, according to people familiar with the matter.

item.title: Manipal Health Set for Muted Mumbai Debut After $960 Million IPO
item.description: Manipal Health Enterprises Ltd. is set for a muted stock market debut in Mumbai after its $960 million initial public offering, as gray market trading signals cooling investor sentiment.

item.title: Chinese Optical Stocks Slide on Report of Proposed US Import Ban
item.description: Zhongji Innolight Co. led losses in Chinese optical stocks after Reuters reported that the US is drafting a ban on imports of some Chinese data center components to protect AI infrastructure.

item.title: Goldman-Backed Biotech Attovia Raises $289 Million in US IPO
item.description: Attovia Therapeutics Inc., an early-stage drug developer focused on immune system diseases with high unmet need, raised $289 million in a US initial public offering that priced at the top of its marketed range.

item.title: Philippine Inflation Slows a Third Month, Easing Pressure for Rate Hike
item.description: Philippine inflation eased for a third month in July, giving the central bank room to assess incoming data and the impact of recent tightening as it weighs whether to raise interest rates.

item.title: Australian Stocks Hit Record High on Iran Hopes, Economic Bets
item.description: Australia’s stock benchmark briefly climbed to an intraday record on easing concerns over the US-Iran conflict and supportive signals in the domestic economy.

item.title: Fed’s Schmid Says Tighter Policy Needed to Reduce Inflation
item.description: Federal Reserve Bank of Kansas City President Jeff Schmid suggested higher interest rates are needed to achieve the Fed’s price stability goals, and reiterated that inflation is his primary concern.

item.title: China’s Quant Curbs Sap Volatility and Turnover: Equity Insight
item.description: China’s latest initiative to rein in quantitative trading is proving something of a double-edged sword for the stock market as it has reduced volatility, but also sapped turnover.

item.title: Gold Holds Steady as Progress on Hormuz Trims Rate-Hike Bets
item.description: Gold traded in a narrow range, as the prospect of an interim deal to reopen the Strait of Hormuz eased inflation concerns and reduced the odds of the US Federal Reserve raising interest rates.

item.title: Australia to Cut Price of Rooftop Solar for Factories, AFR Says
item.description: Australia will cut the price of installing solar panels on warehouse and factory rooftops, the Australian Financial Review reported, in the latest move by the government to accelerate the rollout of green energy.

item.title: Japan’s Nominal Wages Rise Again, Backing BOJ Rate Hike Case
item.description: Japanese wage growth remained firm on the back of solid corporate earnings and a tight labor market, bolstering the case for another Bank of Japan interest rate hike in coming months.

item.title: SoftBank Earnings to Test Appetite for AI Bets Beyond ChatGPT
item.description: SoftBank Group Corp.’s stock faces a critical test this week as investors seek reassurance that the company’s AI value extends beyond its debt-fueled bet on embattled ChatGPT operator OpenAI.

item.title: Lab Monkeys for $26,000 Show China’s Biotech Quest to Rival US
item.description: Prices of lab monkeys in China have surged, complicating new drug development trials and increasing the need for primate imports from neighboring countries.

item.title: New Zealand Unemployment Reaches 11-Year High on Fuel Shock
item.description: New Zealand’s jobless rate rose to an 11-year high in the second quarter as the global energy shock squeezed company profits while more people sought work.

item.title: Coupang’s Losses Grow After Fallout From Data Breach Deepens
item.description: Coupang Inc. reported a larger-than-expected loss, underscoring the damage from a massive personal data leak that resulted in heavy administrative fines in South Korea, its primary market.

item.title: Asian Stocks Set to Advance, Oil Drops on Iran: Markets Wrap
item.description: Asian stocks were set to track Wall Street higher after optimism over a possible interim deal between Washington and Tehran eased concerns about energy supplies, lifting the S&P 500 Index to a record close. Oil fell and bonds gained.

item.title: Booking Holdings Keeps Full-Year Outlook on Resilient Travel
item.description: Booking Holdings Inc. maintained its full-year outlook for gross bookings and revenue due to resilient travel demand even as the Middle East conflict weighs on flight prices and capacity.

item.title: Latest Oil Market News and Analysis for Aug. 5
item.description: Oil held a two-day drop on optimism a deal can be reached that would reopen the Strait of Hormuz.

item.title: OpenAI, Anthropic AI Models Involved in More Security Incidents
item.description: Artificial intelligence models from OpenAI and Anthropic were involved in previously unreported cybersecurity incidents, marking the latest in a recent string of these events.

item.title: Whale Rock Sank 22% as AI Selloff Crippled Hedge Fund Returns
item.description: Whale Rock Capital Management’s flagship hedge fund is one of the biggest losers in last month’s AI selloff, with a 21.7% drop in July erasing about half of its gains for the year.

item.title: Compass Shares Jump on Cost Savings, Transaction Growth
item.description: Compass Inc. shares jumped as much as 15% in post-market trading after the real estate services firm said cost savings from the acquisition of competitor Anywhere were progressing ahead of schedule.

item.title: Wynn’s New Middle Eastern Resort to Open in September 2027
item.description: Wynn Resorts Ltd. said its first casino located in the Middle East will now open in September of next year.
